newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW-CMS sees sustained 15 pct growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-CMS sees sustained 15 pct growth.

text.p: CMS Energy Corp president and chief operating officer Victor Fryling said Thursday he expects the Michigan-based company to sustain 15 percent growth for the next five years, with overseas operations continuing to outpace domestic gains.

"We see 15 percent sustainable annual growth for CMS Energy, as defined by a combination of earnings growth per share and dividend yield, for the next five years," Fryling told Reuters in a telephone interview.
CMS Energy in August raised its common share quarterly dividend to $0.27 from $0.24 paid in the first half of 1996.
It announced Wednesday its earnings per share for the past 12 months rose to $2.45, against $2.27 for 1995.
Total operating revenue reached $4.33 billion in 1996, compared with $3.89 billion in 1995, on the back of assets the company valued at $8.6 billion.
"In 1997, the vast majority of our revenue growth will come from international operations," Fryling said.
"Internationally, the group can sustain growth of 20 percent for the next five years. And, quite frankly, I think we can do better than that," he said.
For 1996, CMS Energy posted $138 million in pre-tax operating income from foreign operations.
This 35 percent increase from 1995 was a key contributor to a nearly 18 percent rise in its net 1996 income, which hit $240 million, compared with $204 million the previous year.

Fryling said the group's 1996 pre-tax operating income from exploration rose to $39 million from $30 million in 1995, its independent power genration brought in $68 million against $46 million in 1995, and overseas pipeline/marketing operations doubled to $28 million from $14 million.
Five years ago, CMS Energy's foreign operating income totalled about $10 million, he said.

Fryling said prices last year for CMS's oil production averaged $17.34/barrel and natural gas prices averaged $2.11/million cubic feet, adding they are using about the same price levels in their 1997 budget planning and earnings forecasts.

Oil output, mostly overseas, totaled 4.6 million barrels per day, up 7.7 percent from 4.3 million in 1995, while gas production, mainly domestic, rose 11.5 percent last year to 29.4 billion cubic feet from 26.3 billion a year earlier.

Among CMS's main overseas projects in 1997 are its Jorf Lasfar coal-fired power plant in Morocco, the country's first privitized power plant, which is to be operated by CMS in a 50-50 joint venture with ASEA-Brown Bovari.
The project's first phase will put 660 megawatts on the market from two generating units while a second phase will boost output to 1,320 MW by 2001 from two additional units.
Other overseas projects CMS plans to add this year include a 230 MW plant in India, a 120 MW plant in Argentina, and the start of the Atacama project in South America.

Atacama involves laying an 800-km (560-mile) gas line from Argentina over the Andes to Chile, where the gas will fire turbines at a 400 MW power plant, scheduled to come on line in January 1999 and providing electricity to local copper mines.
On the domestic front, Fryling said growth in CMS's biggest subsidiary, Consumers Energy, is expected to continue at an annual rate of about two percent.
Consumers Energy, whose service area covers almost all of the lower Michigan penninsula except Detroit, has about three million customers, evenly divided between gas and electricity.

Asked where CMS sees its main growth this year in the U.S., Fryling replied "We are aggressively pursuing natural gas in the lower 48 states," adding they are expanding their gas pipeline network, storage, and processing facilities.
"But our biggest move will be to consolidate our gas and power marketing services and trading unit."

Fryling said the company plans to push hard a strategy that places energy management services at customer sites, an arrangement it already uses in managing energy purchases for General Motors Corp at several of GM's Michigan production facilities.
--James Jelter, New York Power Desk 212-859-1621
